1155-the-secret-adversary.title: The Secret Adversary
1155-the-secret-adversary.creator: Agatha Christie
1155-the-secret-adversary.description: A book by Agatha Christie. She had noticed the speaker more than once amongst the first-class passengers. There had been a hint of mystery about him which had appealed to her imagination. If anyone spoke to him he was quick to rebuff the overture. Also he had a nervous way of looking over his shoulder with a swift, suspicious glance.

arxiv-2108-10265.title: Exploring Biases and Prejudice of Facial Synthesis via Semantic Latent Space
arxiv-2108-10265.creator: Xuyang Shen Jo Plested Sabrina Caldwell Tom Gedeon
arxiv-2108-10265.description: Abstract Deep learning (DL) models are widely used to provide a more convenient and smarter life. However, biased algorithms will negatively influence us. For instance, groups targeted by biased algorithms will feel unfairly treated and even fearful of negative consequences of these biases. This work targets biased generative models’ behaviors, identifying the cause of the biases and eliminating them.

arxiv-2207-03948.title: Self-Adjusting Linear Networks with Ladder Demand Graph
arxiv-2207-03948.creator: Vitaly Aksenov, Anton Paramonov, Iosif Salem, Stefan Schmid
arxiv-2207-03948.description: Abstract Self-adjusting networks (SANs) have the ability to adapt to communication demand by dynamically adjusting the workload (or demand) embedding, i.e., the mapping of communication requests into the network topology. SANs can thus reduce routing costs for frequently communicating node pairs by paying a cost for adjusting the embedding.

arxiv-2406-19140.title: Phonon dynamics in the site-disordered Kitaev spin liquid
arxiv-2406-19140.creator: Vitor Dantas, Wen-Han Kao, Natalia B. Perkins
arxiv-2406-19140.description: Abstract The Kitaev honeycomb model provides a paradigmatic example of an exactly solvable quantum spin liquid (QSL), in which the spin degrees of freedom fractionalize into itinerant Majorana fermions coupled to a static background of ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} gauge fluxes.

arxiv-2409-05748.title: Formation of Close-in Neptunes Around Low-Mass Stars Through Breaking Resonant Chains
arxiv-2409-05748.creator: Donald Liveoak, Sarah C. Millholland
arxiv-2409-05748.description: Abstract Conventional planet formation theories predict a paucity of massive planets around small stars, especially very low-mass ( 0.1 − 0.3 ​ M ⊙ 0.1-0.3\ M_{\odot} ) mid-to-late M dwarfs. Such tiny stars are expected to form planets of terrestrial sizes, but not much bigger.

arxiv-2409-12757.title: A comprehensive theory for relativistic polaritonic chemistry: a four components ab initio treatment of molecular systems coupled to quantum fields
arxiv-2409-12757.creator: Guillaume Thiam, Riccardo Rossi, Henrik Koch, Leonardo Belpassi, Enrico Ronca
arxiv-2409-12757.description: Abstract We present a new ab initio approach to study molecules containing heavy atoms strongly interacting with quantum fields in optical devices. The theory has been derived from the relativistic quantum electrodynamics (QED) introducing the approximations needed to provide a formalism suitable for relativistic quantum chemistry.

arxiv-2412-08295.title: Koszul Lie Algebras and their subalgebras
arxiv-2412-08295.creator: S. Blumer
arxiv-2412-08295.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by S. Blumer. This paper examines (restricted) Koszul Lie algebras, a class of positively graded Lie algebras with a quadratic presentation and specific cohomological properties. The study employs HNN-extensions as a key tool for decomposing and analysing these algebras. Building on a previous work on Koszul Lie algebras [ 4 ] , this paper also deals with Bloch-Kato Lie algebras, which constitute a distinguished subclass of that of Koszul Lie algebras where all subalgebras generated by elements of degree 1 1 have a quadratic presentation.

arxiv-2501-15524.title: Revisiting the outer-weakly convex domination number in graph products
arxiv-2501-15524.creator: Bijo S. Anand, Ullas Chandran S. V, Jonecis A. Dayap, Leomarich F. Casinillo, Karen Luz P. Yap
arxiv-2501-15524.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bijo S. Anand, Ullas Chandran S. V, Jonecis A. Dayap, Leomarich F. Casinillo, Karen Luz P. Yap. Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be a simple undirected graph. A set C ⊆ V ⁡ ( G ) C\subseteq V(G) is weakly convex of graph G G if for every two vertices u , v ∈ G u,v\in G , there exists a u − v u-v geodesic whose vertices are in C C .

arxiv-2508-02882.title: Neural Networks with Orthogonal Jacobian
arxiv-2508-02882.creator: Alex Massucco, Davide Murari, Carola-Bibiane Schönlieb
arxiv-2508-02882.description: Abstract Very deep neural networks achieve state-of-the-art performance by extracting rich, hierarchical features. Yet, training them via backpropagation is often hindered by vanishing or exploding gradients. Existing remedies—such as orthogonal or variance‑preserving initialisation and residual architectures—allow for a more stable gradient propagation and the training of deeper models.

nasa-tm-19720017059-a-procedure-for-pred.title: A procedure for predicting internal and external noise fields of blowdown wind tunnels
nasa-tm-19720017059-a-procedure-for-pred.creator: Unknown
nasa-tm-19720017059-a-procedure-for-pred.description: NASA technical report. The noise generated during the operation of large blowdown wind tunnels is considered. Noise calculation procedures are given to predict the test-section overall and spectrum level noise caused by both the tunnel burner and turbulent boundary layer. External tunnel noise levels d

plos-pone-0007930.title: Lrp4, a Novel Receptor for Dickkopf 1 and Sclerostin, Is Expressed by Osteoblasts and Regulates Bone Growth and Turnover In Vivo
plos-pone-0007930.creator: Hong Y. Choi, Marco Dieckmann, Joachim Herz et al.
plos-pone-0007930.description: PLOS ONE research article. Lrp4 is a multifunctional member of the low density lipoprotein-receptor gene family and a modulator of extracellular cell signaling pathways in development. For example, Lrp4 binds Wise, a secreted Wnt modulator and BMP antagonist. Lrp4 shares structural elements within the extr

pmc-10591743.title: O016 Caregivers’ Perspectives on the Sonomat as a Polysomnography Alternative in Children with Down syndrome
pmc-10591743.creator: K Sclip, A Collaro, J Chawla
pmc-10591743.description: IntroductionChildren with Down syndrome (DS) frequently require repeated polysomnography (PSG) to diagnose and monitor sleep disordered breathing (SDB). PSG set-up can be distressing for this population, who may struggle with sensor and lead application. The Sonomat, a non-invasive mattress overlay, has now been shown to accurately detect and profile SDB in this population.

pmc-10621756.title: Outcomes of Hallux Valgus Corrective Osteotomy: A Tertiary Hospital Experience
pmc-10621756.creator: Ali S Alshehri, Faisal A Alzahrani, Ziad A Aljaafri, Nada A Shalash
pmc-10621756.description: Background: A common form of forefoot deformity, hallux valgus (HV) is characterized by a prominent first metatarsal head, lateral deviation of the hallux, and medial deviation of the first metatarsal bone. In the case of HV, corrective osteotomies are performed with good results and patient satisfaction.

pmc-11326665.title: Initial Experience of Pancreaticoduodenectomy in a Newly Developed Hepato-Pancreato-Biliary Unit Serving in a Lower-Middle-Income Country
pmc-11326665.creator: Neelma, Azwa Rashid, Muhammad Waqas, Muhammad Hammad Ur Rehman, Asad Ullah Khan, Syed Irfan Kabir
pmc-11326665.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction:Pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) is the only potentially curative treatment for pancreatic head adenocarcinoma. This study aimed to determine the short-term outcomes of PD performed over 1 year at a newly established hepato-pancreatico-biliary unit in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan.Material and Methods:A retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained hospital information system (HIS) was undertaken of all patients referred to the unit between May 2021 and August 2022. Data were collected from the medical records of patients in the HIS.

pmc-11344801.title: Constraint-based modelling predicts metabolic signatures of low and high-grade serous ovarian cancer
pmc-11344801.creator: Kate E. Meeson, Jean-Marc Schwartz
pmc-11344801.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Ovarian cancer is an aggressive, heterogeneous disease, burdened with late diagnosis and resistance to chemotherapy. Clinical features of ovarian cancer could be explained by investigating its metabolism, and how the regulation of specific pathways links to individual phenotypes. Ovarian cancer is of particular interest for metabolic research due to its heterogeneous nature, with five distinct subtypes having been identified, each of which may display a unique metabolic signature.

pmc-11595513.title: Experimental Research on the Possibility of Changing the Adhesion of Epoxy Glue to Concrete
pmc-11595513.creator: Andrzej Szewczak, Grzegorz Łagód, Eddie Koenders
pmc-11595513.description: Among the many methods of joining different materials, gluing is characterized by its most specific nature. In comparison with, for example, welded, screwed, or overlapped connections, a glued connection depends on the largest number of factors. Many of them are related to the phenomenon of adhesion, which is complicated by definition.

pmc-11655321.title: Multiple-agent promotion in a grocery store: effects of modality and variability of agents on customer memory
pmc-11655321.creator: Takato Mizuho, Yuki Okafuji, Jun Baba, Takuji Narumi
pmc-11655321.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The use of social robots for product advertising is becoming prevalent. Previous studies have demonstrated that social robots can positively impact ad hoc sales recommendations. However, the essential question of “how effectively customers remember the advertised content” remains unexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a field study where physical robots or virtual agents were stationed at two locations within a grocery store for product promotion.

pmc-12471968.title: Deterioration of Concrete Under the Combined Action of Sulfate Attack and Freeze–Thaw Cycles: A Review
pmc-12471968.creator: Hairong Wu, Chenjie Lv, Youliang Xu, Yuzhou Sun, Songzhao Qu, Xiangming Zhou, Sukhoon Pyo
pmc-12471968.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The synergistic interaction between freeze–thaw cycles and sulfate attack induces a more severe and complex deterioration mechanism in concrete than either factor in isolation. This review elucidates this process by first examining the individual damage mechanisms and then integrating current research to analyze the coupled effects, revealing a complex process involving the superposition and competition of physical crystallization, chemical reactions, and fatigue stresses.

pmc-12514089.title: Toxicity and mechanistic analysis of di(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate in renal cell carcinoma progression: a systematic study with network toxicology and molecular docking strategies
pmc-12514089.creator: Biao Ran, Xinyi Wang, Bohan Liu, Junjiang Ye, Liangren Liu, Zhaofa Yin, Zhongli Huang
pmc-12514089.description: Millions of tons of unrecycled plastic pollute landfills and oceans, and di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP), a plasticizer classified as a possible carcinogen, is found in many environments, and poses health risks. Renal cell carcinoma (RCC), one of the most prevalent malignancies, accounted for approximately 434,419 new cases and 155,702 deaths in 2022.

pmc-12572719.title: Clinical features of influenza-associated pulmonary aspergillosis: a retrospective multicenter cohort study
pmc-12572719.creator: Jia-Xin Shi, Xiang-Rong Shao, Peng Wu, Xiang Wang, Kui Sheng, Qi-Chao Chen, Feng Jin
pmc-12572719.description: RationaleInfluenza-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (IAPA) is a great clinical challenge, which has high morbidity and mortality in severe influenza infections. Unlike invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA), IAPA often occurs in immunocompetent hosts. That IAPA lacks of specific manifestations makes it difficult to diagnose and causes a high mortality rate, which is becoming challenges toclinicians.

pmc-12730957.title: Temporal Changes in Brain Light Scattering and Its Independent Variables Within 2 Days of Life
pmc-12730957.creator: Kennosuke Tsuda, Sachiko Iwata, Shinji Saitoh, Osuke Iwata
pmc-12730957.description: The reduced scattering coefficient (μs′), measured using time-resolved near-infrared spectroscopy (TR-NIRS) has been linked to brain water diffusion assessed by diffusion tensor imaging, suggesting its potential as a bedside marker of cerebral microstructure. However, the physiological determinants of μs′ and its early postnatal changes remain unclear.

pmc-12749944.title: An assessment of the effect of external window shading on heating and cooling loads in buildings in Iraq
pmc-12749944.creator: Bashir Eskander Kareem
pmc-12749944.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). External shading devices are critical for improving the energy performance of buildings, particularly in hot climates. Effective design must allow beneficial solar gains during winter while minimizing heat ingress in summer. This study systematically evaluates overhangs, left fins, and right fins on windows with varying orientations in Erbil, Iraq, using the hourly analysis program to quantify solar radiation reduction and corresponding energy savings.

pmc-12985007.title: Chronic consumption of energy drinks and the risk of developing metabolic syndrome in rats
pmc-12985007.creator: Ahlam Saleh Alhajri
pmc-12985007.description: The consumption of energy drinks (EDs) has notably increased, particularly among adolescents and young adults, due to their perceived benefits in enhancing physical and cognitive performance. However, growing evidence points to their potential adverse health effects, raising concerns regarding their safety. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the metabolic impacts of three commercially available EDs on male albino rats.

pmc-13013482.title: Comparative performance of hrHPV testing and PAX1/ZNF671 methylation in triaging women with abnormal cytology: a study of paired urine, vaginal and cervical scrape samples
pmc-13013482.creator: Yuanyuan Wang, Lufang Zhang, Hongke Zhao, Derong Guo, Huimin Guo, Mengwei Miao, Haixia Qin, Ying Liu
pmc-13013482.description: BackgroundThe purpose was to evaluate the diagnostic effectiveness of High-risk human papillomavirus(hrHPV) testing, DNA methylation, PAX1/ZNF671 methylation in triaging patients with abnormal cytology and/or abnormal cervical biopsy pathology in cervical cancer screening; And the detection performance of different screening strategies was compared among clinician-taken cervical scrapes and paired self-collected urine and vaginal samples.

pmc-13100966.title: Development and validation of a predictive model for depression risk in older patients with multiple chronic diseases in the community: cross-sectional study based on a health ecology model
pmc-13100966.creator: Zhirong Xu, Wen Ding, Jing Zhao, Guolian Liu, Hui Wan
pmc-13100966.description: AimGuided by the health ecology model, which posits that an individual’s health is shaped by the dynamic interplay between personal and environmental factors, we investigated factors associated with depression in community-dwelling older adults with multimorbidity and developed a nomogram-based risk prediction model.

pmc-13240758.title: Intermediate alar resection: Precision technique for nasal tip aesthetics
pmc-13240758.creator: Goran Latif Omer, Sureyya Şeneldir, Sahand Soran Ali, Giuseppe De Donato, Andrea Gravina, Sveva Viola, Gaia Grasso, Maria Grazia Maglie, Heshu Sulaiman Rahman, Othman Hussein, Aso Khasraw, Stefano Di Girolamo
pmc-13240758.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effectiveness of a newly described rhinoplasty technique, Intermediate Alar Resection (IAR), designed to refine the nasal tip by selectively modifying the intermediate crura.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 52 patients undergoing primary rhinoplasty with IAR between January 2024 and June 2025 was analysed.

pmc-13253888.title: Lessons from Denmark for community-based governance of urban heat networks
pmc-13253888.creator: Eirini Sampson, Zen Makuch

pmc-13515775.title: Thermal Processing and Fortification with Ayocote and Quintonil Flours Affect Blue Maize Tortilla and Tortilla Chip Properties
pmc-13515775.creator: Edwin Rojo-Gutiérrez, Leticia Xochitl López-Martínez, Mónica Alejandra Villegas-Ochoa, Ezequiel Muñoz-Márquez, Ramiro Baeza-Jiménez
pmc-13515775.description: Modern food systems face the challenge of improving nutritional quality while reducing environmental impact and conserving agrobiodiversity. This study evaluated the effects of thermal processing and fortification with ayocote (Phaseolus coccineus) and quintonil (Amaranthus hybridus) flours on the physicochemical, nutritional, and functional properties of blue maize tortillas, baked tortilla chips (BTCs), and fried tortilla chips (FTCs).

pmc-13523680.title: Evaluation of an Adapted Murine Electrolytic Model of Venous Injury in Wistar Rats: Histopathological Characterization and Challenges in Model Adaptation
pmc-13523680.creator: Emma Eugenia Murariu-Gligor, Bogdan Cordoș, Andreea-Raluca Cozac-Szőke, Alexandru Nicușor Tomuț, Ovidiu S Cotoi, Simona Mureșan
pmc-13523680.description: IntroductionMurine models are widely used in deep vein thrombosis biomedical studies. The principal large-vessel models include ligature-based and free radical thrombosis models (e.g., the ferric chloride or electrolytic models), with the inferior vena cava and femoral vein being the most commonly used vessels.

pmc-13597863.title: Laparoscopic versus open emergency repair for strangulated abdominal wall hernias: a propensity-score-matched retrospective cohort study
pmc-13597863.creator: Ahmet Topcu, İsmail Ege Subaşı, Furkan Saydin
pmc-13597863.description: Background and objectivesThe optimal surgical approach for incarcerated or strangulated abdominal wall hernias remains debated. While laparoscopic techniques are well established electively, evidence on their emergency-setting role is limited. This study compared open and laparoscopic repair in patients undergoing emergency surgery for incarcerated or strangulated abdominal wall hernias, focusing on postoperative morbidity, mortality, operative time, and hospital stay.
